title: A rating transition matrix and its two-year evolution
source:
"""One-year transition matrix from counts, and the two-year Markov matrix P @ P.

Rows are normalised to probability distributions. Default is absorbing: the D
row is set to certainty of staying in D whatever the counts say (a firm in
default cannot migrate). The matrix product needs rows and columns in the SAME
rating order, so rows are aligned to the column order before multiplying and
written back in the input's row order.
"""
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

INPUT = "/input/environment/data/transition_counts.csv"
OUT_DIR = "/app/output"


def main() -> None:
    counts = pd.read_csv(INPUT)
    ratings = [c for c in counts.columns if c != "from_rating"]
    m = counts.set_index("from_rating").loc[ratings, ratings].astype(float)

    row_sums = m.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    p = m.to_numpy() / np.where(row_sums > 0, row_sums, 1.0)[:, None]
    d = ratings.index("D")
    p[d, :] = 0.0
    p[d, d] = 1.0
    p2 = p @ p

    for name, mat in (("transition_1y.csv", p), ("transition_2y.csv", p2)):
        assert np.allclose(mat.sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=1e-12), f"{name} rows must sum to 1"
        assert mat[d, d] == 1.0 and np.allclose(np.delete(mat[d], d), 0.0), "D must stay absorbing"
        frame = pd.DataFrame(mat, index=ratings, columns=ratings).loc[list(counts["from_rating"])]
        frame.insert(0, "from_rating", list(counts["from_rating"]))
        os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
        frame.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, name), index=False, float_format="%.17g")
        back = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, name))
        assert list(back.columns) == ["from_rating"] + ratings and len(back) == len(counts)
    print("ok", ratings)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
